title: {Syn} Euclid Algorithm Is Ancient and Still Fast
content:
The Euclidean algorithm computes the greatest common divisor by repeatedly replacing the larger number with its remainder after division by the smaller one. It is one of the oldest algorithms still taught in modern computer science.

Its extended form also finds integers x and y such that ax + by equals gcd(a,b), which is exactly the tool needed for modular inverses.

Why it matters: algorithms keeps producing ideas that are simple enough to state and strong enough to build with.
